comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral characterization (C1, C11-C20). Both evaluations find the stimulus-response patterns, quantitative analysis, and behavioral measurements compelling and well-supported with no concerns raised.

Complete agreement on CR neuron identification (C21-C27). Both evaluations accept the morphological and physiological characterization of receptor neurons through electron microscopy and calcium imaging as compelling evidence.

Strong agreement on gene expression patterns (C28-C31). OpenEval finds expression data well-supported; peer reviewers recognize the genetic demonstration as compelling. Peer review includes C2 while OpenEval does not, but both accept the molecular characterization.

Divergent evaluations of CRISPR mutant data (C32-C36). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on complete loss of function with preserved morphology. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional calcium imaging in mutants and rescue experiments, with concerns about PKD-2 broader expression affecting specificity (C3 included in peer review).

Divergent evaluations of predation experiments (C4, C37-C39). OpenEval finds ecological validation SUPPORTED despite acknowledging correlative nature. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, specifically requesting PKD1-1 mutant predation assays to address specificity concerns about PKD-2-expressing neurons.

Divergent evaluations of circuit connectivity (C5, C40-C48). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment that some functional inferences await validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing circuit mechanisms are 'plausible models' requiring systematic ablation/inactivation experiments and requesting primary EM data figures. Peer review also includes motoneuron claims C49-C59.

Partial overlap on motoneuron circuit mapping (C49-C59). OpenEval evaluates motoneuron connectivity separately as SUPPORTED with calcium imaging validation. Peer reviewers group this with broader circuit claims (R6) and rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting functional validation beyond receptor level.

Agreement on mechanotransduction interpretation (C60-C66). Both evaluations accept the inference that PKD proteins function in mechanotransduction based on preserved morphology in mutants. OpenEval notes direct mechanistic evidence would strengthen conclusions; peer reviewers note a discussion gap regarding C. elegans circuits but don't challenge the core interpretation.

Agreement on uncertainty of circuit mechanisms (C69-C75, C77). Both evaluations rate mechanistic interpretations as UNCERTAIN/plausible models lacking direct functional validation. OpenEval emphasizes need for selective activation/silencing; peer reviewers state mechanisms are 'limited to plausible models' requiring experimental validation.

Agreement on uncertainty of pathway specialization (C79-C80). Both evaluations find these hypotheses UNCERTAIN, lacking direct experimental validation through pathway-specific manipulations. Peer reviewers group with broader circuit mechanism concerns.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty of bilateral coordination mechanisms (C82-C85). Both evaluations rate these as UNCERTAIN/plausible models based on anatomical observations without functional testing of proposed coordination strategies.

Agreement on basic morphological descriptions (C9-C10). Both evaluations accept these descriptive claims as SUPPORTED. Peer review also includes C7-C8 in this group while OpenEval places those in R13.
Agreement on ecological context citations (C67-C68, C71-C72). Both evaluations accept these contextual claims based on literature as SUPPORTED, providing accepted background for ecological relevance.

Agreement on comparative framework citations (C75-C76, C78, C81, C86-C88). Both evaluations accept these comparative claims as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note the work represents a rare complete circuit description but identify omission of C. elegans escape circuits as a gap.

Partial overlap on background claims (C7-C8). OpenEval groups these with extensive citation-based claims as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers group C7-C8 with basic morphological descriptions (C9-C10), also rating as SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluation of main integrative conclusion (C6). OpenEval rates the synthesis of genetic, behavioral, circuit, and ecological evidence as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers' UNCERTAIN rating of circuit mechanisms and predation specificity suggests the integrative conclusion may be premature pending additional validation experiments.
